title: 2010 AMC 12B Problem 9
statement: Let \(n\) be the smallest positive integer such that \(n\) is divisible by \(20,\) \(n^2\) is a perfect cube, and \(n^3\) is a perfect square. What is the number of digits of \(n?\)

solutions.text:
To be smallest, \(n\) uses only the primes of \(20,\) so \(n=2^a\cdot5^b\) with \(a\ge2\) and \(b\ge1.\)

Since \(n^2=2^{2a}5^{2b}\) is a perfect cube, \(a\) and \(b\) are multiples of \(3.\) Since \(n^3=2^{3a}5^{3b}\) is a perfect square, \(a\) and \(b\) are multiples of \(2.\) Hence \(a\) and \(b\) are multiples of \(6.\)

The smallest choice is \(a=b=6,\) so \(n=2^6\cdot5^6=10^6=1{,}000{,}000,\) which has \(7\) digits.

Thus, the correct answer is E.
hints: Write \(n=2^a\cdot5^b;\) any extra prime factor only makes \(n\) larger
\(n^2\) a cube forces \(a\) and \(b\) to be multiples of \(3;\) \(n^3\) a square forces \(a\) and \(b\) to be multiples of \(2\)
